newsitem.title: CHINA: Natural disasters cost China 230 bln yuan in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Natural disasters cost China 230 bln yuan in 1996.

text.p: Flooding, drought, earthquakes and other natural disasters in China caused direct losses of 230 billion yuan ($27.7 billion) in 1996, the Economic Information Daily said on Wednesday.
Average economic losses caused by natural disasters in the 1990s was more than 100 billion yuan a year, compared with 50-60 billion yuan a year in the 1970s and 1980s, the newspaper said.
Floods and drought accounted for 57 percent of total losses from 1950 to 1996, while earthquakes were the deadliest natural calamity, accounting for 51 percent of natural disaster deaths, it said.
State media has said flooding caused more than 200 billion yuan in damages in 1996 and that natural disasters affected more than 300 million people last year.
This year, flooding across much of southern and central China have killed at least 284 people and destroyed or damaged hundreds of thousands of homes, international aid workers said last week.
Several earthquakes have also struck the northwestern region of Xinjiang, killing dozens of people and flattening tens of thousands of homes and buildings.
Natural disasters killed 68 people and caused 1.73 billion yuan in property damage in the first three months of this year, state media has said.
China's largest insurer, the People's Insurance Group, was expected to pay out a total of 3.7 billion yuan in compensation for flood-related damage last year, earlier figures show.
